title: Lake Manyara National Park: A Small Park With Variety
excerpt: Lake Manyara is a small park at the foot of the Rift Valley wall, with groundwater forest, a soda lake and lots of birdlife.
body:
Lake Manyara National Park lies at the foot of the Great Rift Valley escarpment, on the way from Arusha to Ngorongoro. It is small, but varied.

## Landscapes

- Groundwater forest near the entrance, with tall trees and baboons.
- Acacia woodland.
- Open grassland along the lake.
- The alkaline lake itself, with flamingos and pelicans at times.
- Hot springs in the south.

## Wildlife

Elephants, giraffes, buffaloes, zebras, hippos and large troops of olive baboons. Lions are present; Manyara is famous for [tree-climbing lions](/blog/tree-climbing-lions-manyara/), though sightings are not guaranteed.

## Birds

More than 400 species have been recorded. Good for birdwatchers.

## How long

A half day or full day. Many travellers visit on the way to Ngorongoro.

## Treetop walkway

A treetop walkway in the forest has been available in the past; ask us whether it is operating.

## Village stop

The village of [Mto wa Mbu](/blog/mto-wa-mbu-village/) just outside the park is a good place for a cultural walk.

Read our [Lake Manyara page](/national-parks/lake-manyara/) or [plan your safari](/travel-proposal/).
